paragraphs.title: The People Ask for a God and Make a Calf

easy.question: Why did the people gather around Aaron?
answers: Because Moses delayed coming down from the mountain
Because Aaron left the camp
Because the Egyptians came to chase them again
easy.explanation: The people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, so they gathered around Aaron.

easy.question: What did the people ask Aaron to do?
answers: Build them a house
Make them gods to go before them
Take them back to Egypt
easy.explanation: The people told Aaron, “Up, make us gods, which shall go before us.”

easy.question: What were the calf and its image made from?
answers: Mountain stones
Wood
Golden earrings
easy.explanation: The people brought their golden earrings, and Aaron made a molten calf from them.

medium.question: What did the people do after Aaron asked them to bring their golden earrings?
answers: They removed their golden earrings and brought them to Aaron
They waited for Moses
They returned to the wilderness
medium.explanation: After Aaron’s request, the people removed their golden earrings and brought them to him.

medium.question: What did the people say they did not know about Moses?
answers: Where he had gone
Why he left Egypt
Whether he was leading the Egyptians
medium.explanation: They said they did not know what had become of Moses, the man who had brought them out of Egypt.

medium.question: How did uncertainty about Moses affect the people’s actions?
answers: They decided to wait quietly
They sent people to search for him in Egypt
They asked Aaron to make something to go before them
medium.explanation: Because they did not know what had happened to Moses, they asked for a visible god and leader.

challenge.question: What does the people’s statement, “These be thy gods,” show about what they claimed the calf had done?
answers: They credited the calf with bringing them out of Egypt
They knew Moses would return immediately
They were speaking only about Aaron
challenge.explanation: The people attributed the exodus from Egypt to the calf, treating it as their god or gods.

challenge.question: What major change did the gold undergo from the beginning to the end of the process?
answers: It remained with the people’s families
It became an object meant to represent and lead the people
It was returned to its owners shortly afterward
challenge.explanation: The gold began as earrings but was melted and fashioned into a calf that the people treated as a god and leader.

challenge.question: Which conclusion best fits the order of events in these verses?
answers: Aaron alone planned the exodus
Moses gave the people gold to make the calf
Moses’ absence led the people to quickly seek a tangible replacement
challenge.explanation: The people became alarmed by Moses’ delay, requested something to lead them, and then gave Aaron their gold.

questions.question: What does the people’s statement, “These be thy gods,” show about what they claimed the calf had done?
answers: They credited the calf with bringing them out of Egypt
They knew Moses would return immediately
They were speaking only about Aaron
questions.explanation: The people attributed the exodus from Egypt to the calf, treating it as their god or gods.

questions.question: What major change did the gold undergo from the beginning to the end of the process?
answers: It remained with the people’s families
It became an object meant to represent and lead the people
It was returned to its owners shortly afterward
questions.explanation: The gold began as earrings but was melted and fashioned into a calf that the people treated as a god and leader.

questions.question: Which conclusion best fits the order of events in these verses?
answers: Aaron alone planned the exodus
Moses gave the people gold to make the calf
Moses’ absence led the people to quickly seek a tangible replacement
questions.explanation: The people became alarmed by Moses’ delay, requested something to lead them, and then gave Aaron their gold.

paragraphs.title: The People Celebrate before the Calf

easy.question: What did Aaron build before the people?
answers: An altar
A tent
A palace
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it.”

easy.question: For whom did Aaron announce that there would be a feast?
answers: Moses
The Lord
The people of Egypt
easy.explanation: Aaron announced, “To morrow is a feast to the Lord.”

easy.question: What did the people do after they ate and drank?
answers: They went to sleep
They built tents
They rose up to play
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying that they “rose up to play.”

medium.question: What can we understand from Aaron’s words, “To morrow is a feast”?
answers: The feast was planned for the next day
The feast had already ended
The feast took place before the altar was built
medium.explanation: “To morrow” shows that the feast was to take place on the following day.

medium.question: What happened first in the sequence described here?
answers: The people ate before any offerings were made
The people played before the altar was built
The people offered sacrifices before eating and drinking
medium.explanation: They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and afterward sat down to eat and drink.

medium.question: What was the order of events according to the verses?
answers: The people ate, and then they built an altar
The people played, and then they offered burnt offerings
They offered sacrifices, and then they ate and drank
medium.explanation: First they offered burnt and peace offerings; afterward they sat down to eat and drink.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes Aaron’s actions in verse 5?
answers: He saw the calf, built an altar, and announced the feast
He announced the feast, saw the calf, and built an altar
He built an altar, ate, and announced the feast
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the actions in that order: Aaron saw the calf, built an altar, and made an announcement.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the event included both sacrifices and a meal?
answers: The people rose early
They offered burnt and peace offerings, then sat down to eat and drink
Aaron announced a feast
challenge.explanation: The offerings represent worship, while eating and drinking represent the meal.

challenge.question: What change in the people’s behavior occurs from the beginning to the end of the passage?
answers: They moved from sitting and eating to standing in prayer
They moved from rising early to sleeping
They moved from ritual acts to eating, drinking, and playing
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from sacrifices to eating and drinking, and finally to playing.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes Aaron’s actions in verse 5?
answers: He saw the calf, built an altar, and announced the feast
He announced the feast, saw the calf, and built an altar
He built an altar, ate, and announced the feast
questions.explanation: The verse presents the actions in that order: Aaron saw the calf, built an altar, and made an announcement.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the event included both sacrifices and a meal?
answers: The people rose early
They offered burnt and peace offerings, then sat down to eat and drink
Aaron announced a feast
questions.explanation: The offerings represent worship, while eating and drinking represent the meal.

questions.question: What change in the people’s behavior occurs from the beginning to the end of the passage?
answers: They moved from sitting and eating to standing in prayer
They moved from rising early to sleeping
They moved from ritual acts to eating, drinking, and playing
questions.explanation: The passage moves from sacrifices to eating and drinking, and finally to playing.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Tells Moses about the Sin

easy.question: What did the Israelites make instead of worshiping the Lord?
answers: A molten calf
An altar in Jerusalem
A return journey to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Israelites made a molten calf and worshiped it.

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in these verses?
answers: Aaron
Moses
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verses begin with the Lord speaking to Moses.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do to the calf?
answers: They destroyed it
They hid it
They worshiped it and sacrificed to it
easy.explanation: The verse says that they worshiped the calf and sacrificed to it.

medium.question: Why did the Lord tell Moses, “Go, get thee down”?
answers: Because the Israelites had turned aside and made a calf
Because Moses had asked to leave the mountain
Because the people had already reached Canaan
medium.explanation: The Lord told Moses to go down because the people had corrupted themselves and worshiped the calf.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events described in these verses?
answers: The people sacrificed, then made the calf, and finally Moses came down
The people made a calf, worshiped and sacrificed to it, and called it their god
Moses came down, the people returned to the right path, and then made a calf
medium.explanation: First the calf was made; then the people worshiped it and declared it to be their god.

medium.question: What does the Lord’s description of Israel as “stiffnecked” emphasize?
answers: That the people were physically strong
That they were impatient only
That they were stubborn and unwilling to listen
medium.explanation: “Stiffnecked” describes people who are stubborn and unwilling to submit or listen.

challenge.question: What punishment did the Lord propose, and what did he offer to do for Moses afterward?
answers: Destroy the people and make Moses into a great nation
Punish only Aaron and send the people back to Egypt
Forgive the people and make Moses king
challenge.explanation: The Lord said he would consume the people and make a great nation from Moses.

challenge.question: What does “let me alone” mean in the context of the Lord’s anger?
answers: Moses must go up the mountain
Moses was asked not to stop the execution of judgment
The people must leave the camp
challenge.explanation: “Let me alone” means, “Allow me to act”; the Lord was telling Moses not to restrain his judgment.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “turned aside quickly” emphasize?
answers: The people traveled quickly toward Canaan
The people waited a long time before worshiping the calf
The people abandoned the commanded way immediately
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes how quickly Israel abandoned the way the Lord had commanded.

questions.question: What punishment did the Lord propose, and what did he offer to do for Moses afterward?
answers: Destroy the people and make Moses into a great nation
Punish only Aaron and send the people back to Egypt
Forgive the people and make Moses king
questions.explanation: The Lord said he would consume the people and make a great nation from Moses.

questions.question: What does “let me alone” mean in the context of the Lord’s anger?
answers: Moses must go up the mountain
Moses was asked not to stop the execution of judgment
The people must leave the camp
questions.explanation: “Let me alone” means, “Allow me to act”; the Lord was telling Moses not to restrain his judgment.

questions.question: What does the phrase “turned aside quickly” emphasize?
answers: The people traveled quickly toward Canaan
The people waited a long time before worshiping the calf
The people abandoned the commanded way immediately
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes how quickly Israel abandoned the way the Lord had commanded.

easy.question: What did Moses ask the Lord to do?
answers: Turn away from his anger against the people
Return the people to Egypt
Give the people a king
easy.explanation: Moses asked the Lord to turn from his fierce anger and not destroy his people.

easy.question: Whom did Moses remind the Lord of?
answers: Moses, Aaron, and Joshua
Abraham, Isaac, and Israel
Pharaoh, Egypt, and Midian
easy.explanation: Moses reminded the Lord of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom he had sworn his promises.

easy.question: What did the Lord do in the end, according to verse 14?
answers: He punished the people immediately
He sent the people to Egypt
He turned from the evil he had said he would do to his people
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord repented of the evil he had thought to do to his people.

medium.question: What is the correct order of Moses’ argument?
answers: The Lord relented, Moses reminded him of the ancestors, and then Moses prayed
Moses pleaded, reminded the Lord of Egypt and the ancestors, and asked him to change his decision
Moses mentioned Egypt, the people returned there, and the Lord punished them
medium.explanation: Moses pleaded with the Lord, referred to Egypt and the ancestors, and asked him not to carry out the punishment.

medium.question: What does “fierce wrath” mean in the phrase “Turn from thy fierce wrath”?
answers: Great joy
A memory
Intense anger
medium.explanation: “Fierce wrath” refers to powerful anger; Moses was asking the Lord to turn away from it.

medium.question: Why did Moses mention what the Egyptians might say?
answers: To prevent dishonor to the Lord’s name and avert disaster from Israel
To ask permission to return to Egypt
To announce that Egypt had won a battle
medium.explanation: Moses argued that the Egyptians might misunderstand Israel’s destruction, so he asked the Lord not to destroy his people.

challenge.question: Which combination of arguments appears in Moses’ prayer?
answers: The people were completely innocent and should not be punished
The Lord’s reputation among the Egyptians and his promises to the ancestors should both be considered
The Egyptians wanted to join Israel
challenge.explanation: Moses appealed both to the Lord’s reputation among the Egyptians and to his promises and oath to the ancestors.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “by thine own self” mean in Moses’ words?
answers: The ancestors swore to Moses
The Lord swore to the ancestors through Moses
The Lord swore to the ancestors by his own name and person
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord himself made the oath, underscoring his faithfulness to his promise.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from verse 14?
answers: Moses’ prayer had an effect, and the Lord did not carry out the threatened punishment
The Lord forgot his promises to the ancestors
The people immediately left the wilderness
challenge.explanation: After Moses’ plea, the Lord turned from the punishment he had said he would bring.

questions.question: Which combination of arguments appears in Moses’ prayer?
answers: The people were completely innocent and should not be punished
The Lord’s reputation among the Egyptians and his promises to the ancestors should both be considered
The Egyptians wanted to join Israel
questions.explanation: Moses appealed both to the Lord’s reputation among the Egyptians and to his promises and oath to the ancestors.

questions.question: What does the phrase “by thine own self” mean in Moses’ words?
answers: The ancestors swore to Moses
The Lord swore to the ancestors through Moses
The Lord swore to the ancestors by his own name and person
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord himself made the oath, underscoring his faithfulness to his promise.

questions.question: What can we conclude from verse 14?
answers: Moses’ prayer had an effect, and the Lord did not carry out the threatened punishment
The Lord forgot his promises to the ancestors
The people immediately left the wilderness
questions.explanation: After Moses’ plea, the Lord turned from the punishment he had said he would bring.

paragraphs.title: Moses Comes Down with the Tablets

easy.question: What did Moses carry down from the mountain?
answers: The two tablets of the testimony
A scroll of the Law
A staff
easy.explanation: Moses came down with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands.

easy.question: Where was the writing on the tablets?
answers: Only on the front
On both sides
Only on the back
easy.explanation: The verse says that the tablets were written on both sides.

easy.question: Who heard the sound of the people?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: Joshua heard the noise of the people in the camp.

medium.question: What did Joshua initially think he heard in the camp?
answers: The noise of war
The sound of prayer
The sound of weeping
medium.explanation: Joshua said, “There is a noise of war in the camp,” because he understood the sound that way.

medium.question: What does the verse mean by saying that the writing was “graven upon the tables”?
answers: The tablets were broken
The writing was carved into them
The tablets were covered
medium.explanation: The wording shows that the writing was carved or engraved on the tablets.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Joshua heard a sound, Moses went up the mountain, and Moses came down
Moses interpreted the sound, Joshua heard it, and Moses came down
Moses came down with the tablets, Joshua heard a sound, and Moses interpreted it
medium.explanation: Moses first came down with the tablets; Joshua then heard the sound, and Moses explained it.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by saying that the tablets were written “on both their sides”?
answers: The writing covered both sides of the tablets
There were only two sentences on the tablets
Each tablet was written by a different person
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the writing was on both sides, not just one.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses’ reply to Joshua about the sound?
answers: Moses immediately agreed that it was a battle
Moses recognized that it was neither a victory cry nor a cry of defeat
Moses heard no sound at all
challenge.explanation: Moses rejected both explanations and identified the sound as singing or celebration.

challenge.question: Which detail attributes both the tablets and the writing to God?
answers: The tablets were God’s work and the writing was God’s writing
Moses made the tablets himself
Joshua prepared the writing in the camp
challenge.explanation: The verse twice emphasizes their divine origin: the tablets were God’s work and the writing was God’s writing.

questions.question: What is emphasized by saying that the tablets were written “on both their sides”?
answers: The writing covered both sides of the tablets
There were only two sentences on the tablets
Each tablet was written by a different person
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the writing was on both sides, not just one.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses’ reply to Joshua about the sound?
answers: Moses immediately agreed that it was a battle
Moses recognized that it was neither a victory cry nor a cry of defeat
Moses heard no sound at all
questions.explanation: Moses rejected both explanations and identified the sound as singing or celebration.

questions.question: Which detail attributes both the tablets and the writing to God?
answers: The tablets were God’s work and the writing was God’s writing
Moses made the tablets himself
Joshua prepared the writing in the camp
questions.explanation: The verse twice emphasizes their divine origin: the tablets were God’s work and the writing was God’s writing.

paragraphs.title: Moses Breaks the Tablets and Destroys the Calf

easy.question: What did Moses see as he approached the camp?
answers: The calf and dancing
The tablets
The mountain on fire
easy.explanation: Moses saw the calf and the dancing, and his anger became hot.

easy.question: What did Moses do to the tablets?
answers: He hid them
He broke them
He gave them to Israel
easy.explanation: Moses cast the tablets from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.

easy.question: What did Moses do to the calf after taking it?
answers: He kept it in the tent
He gave it to the people
He burned it in the fire
easy.explanation: Moses took the calf and burned it in the fire.

medium.question: Why did Moses’ anger become hot?
answers: Because he saw the calf and the dancing
Because the people climbed the mountain
Because the fire went out
medium.explanation: The text connects Moses’ anger with his seeing the calf and the dancing.

medium.question: What were the people doing around the calf?
answers: Building camps
Dancing
Preparing for war
medium.explanation: The verse says that Moses saw the calf and the dancing.

medium.question: What did Moses do immediately after burning the calf?
answers: He made the Israelites drink
He went up the mountain
He ground it to powder
medium.explanation: After burning the calf, Moses ground it to powder.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses’ burning, grinding, and scattering the calf in water?
answers: He wanted to erase it completely
He wanted to repair it
He intended to preserve it for later
challenge.explanation: The series of actions shows that Moses intended to destroy the calf and remove its significance completely.

challenge.question: What was the correct order of actions after Moses took the calf?
answers: He made the people drink, burned it, ground it, and scattered it
He burned it, ground it, scattered it in water, and made the Israelites drink
He ground it, made the people drink, burned it, and scattered it
challenge.explanation: The verse gives this order: burning, grinding, scattering in water, and making Israel drink it.

challenge.question: What does the statement that Moses “made the children of Israel drink of it” show?
answers: Only Moses drank the water
Only the calf-makers drank it
The Israelites were made to drink the water containing the calf’s powder
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that this action was directed toward the people of Israel.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses’ burning, grinding, and scattering the calf in water?
answers: He wanted to erase it completely
He wanted to repair it
He intended to preserve it for later
questions.explanation: The series of actions shows that Moses intended to destroy the calf and remove its significance completely.

questions.question: What was the correct order of actions after Moses took the calf?
answers: He made the people drink, burned it, ground it, and scattered it
He burned it, ground it, scattered it in water, and made the Israelites drink
He ground it, made the people drink, burned it, and scattered it
questions.explanation: The verse gives this order: burning, grinding, scattering in water, and making Israel drink it.

questions.question: What does the statement that Moses “made the children of Israel drink of it” show?
answers: Only Moses drank the water
Only the calf-makers drank it
The Israelites were made to drink the water containing the calf’s powder
questions.explanation: The wording shows that this action was directed toward the people of Israel.

easy.question: Whom did Moses ask, “What did this people unto thee”?
answers: Aaron
The people
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Moses asked Aaron what the people had done to him.

easy.question: What did the people ask Aaron to make?
answers: An altar
Gods to go before them
A return route to Egypt
easy.explanation: The people told Aaron, “Make us gods, which shall go before us.”

easy.question: What came out of the fire according to Aaron?
answers: A cloud
Gold
The calf
easy.explanation: Aaron claimed, “I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.”

medium.question: What does Aaron mean by “Let not the anger of my lord wax hot”?
answers: Do not be angry, my lord
Do not leave, my lord
Do not speak, my lord
medium.explanation: Aaron was asking Moses not to become angry and was trying to calm him.

medium.question: Why did the people ask Aaron to make them gods?
answers: Because they wanted to celebrate
Because they did not know what had happened to Moses
Because they wanted to return to Egypt
medium.explanation: They said they did not know what had become of Moses, so they asked for gods to lead them.

medium.question: What order of events does Aaron describe?
answers: The people gave him gold, he threw it into the fire, and the calf came out
The calf came out, then the people gave him gold, and he threw it into the fire
Aaron burned the people, and then they made the calf
medium.explanation: Aaron describes the people giving him gold, his throwing it into the fire, and the calf coming out.

challenge.question: What is Aaron trying to suggest by saying, “I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf”?
answers: That he planned to build the calf
That the calf’s creation happened by itself
That the calf existed before the gold
challenge.explanation: Aaron’s wording minimizes his responsibility and makes the calf seem to have emerged on its own.

challenge.question: What relationship between Moses’ words and Aaron’s words is evident?
answers: Moses accuses Aaron, while Aaron tries to defend himself
Moses praises Aaron, while Aaron thanks the people
Moses asks the people for forgiveness, while Aaron remains silent
challenge.explanation: Moses says Aaron brought a great sin upon the people, while Aaron responds with an excuse.

challenge.question: What does Aaron’s statement that the people were “set on mischief” suggest?
answers: The people were always calm and obedient
The people had never known Moses
The people tended toward wrongdoing and were difficult to control
challenge.explanation: Aaron portrays the people as inclined toward evil, using that as an excuse for the pressure they placed on him.

questions.question: What is Aaron trying to suggest by saying, “I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf”?
answers: That he planned to build the calf
That the calf’s creation happened by itself
That the calf existed before the gold
questions.explanation: Aaron’s wording minimizes his responsibility and makes the calf seem to have emerged on its own.

questions.question: What relationship between Moses’ words and Aaron’s words is evident?
answers: Moses accuses Aaron, while Aaron tries to defend himself
Moses praises Aaron, while Aaron thanks the people
Moses asks the people for forgiveness, while Aaron remains silent
questions.explanation: Moses says Aaron brought a great sin upon the people, while Aaron responds with an excuse.

questions.question: What does Aaron’s statement that the people were “set on mischief” suggest?
answers: The people were always calm and obedient
The people had never known Moses
The people tended toward wrongdoing and were difficult to control
questions.explanation: Aaron portrays the people as inclined toward evil, using that as an excuse for the pressure they placed on him.

paragraphs.title: The Levites Stand with the Lord

easy.question: Who gathered to Moses after he called, “Who is on the Lord’s side”?
answers: All the sons of Levi
The elders of the people
Aaron and his sons alone
easy.explanation: The verse says, “All the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.”

easy.question: How many people fell that day?
answers: About one thousand
About three thousand
About ten thousand
easy.explanation: The verse says that about three thousand men fell that day.

easy.question: Where was Moses standing when he called for those who were faithful to the Lord?
answers: At the door of the tent of meeting
On Mount Sinai
At the gate of the camp
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses stood at the gate of the camp.

medium.question: Why did Moses call people to gather to him?
answers: Because the people had become uncontrolled and disgraceful
To choose a new leader
To begin a journey through the wilderness
medium.explanation: Moses saw that the people were unrestrained and that their behavior could bring disgrace upon them.

medium.question: What does the verse mean by saying that the people were “unrestrained”?
answers: They were tired and weak
They had lost discipline and order
They were far from the camp
medium.explanation: The description refers to people who had lost self-control and proper order.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The Levites acted, and then Moses called them
The people left the camp, and then Moses went up the mountain
Moses called, the Levites gathered, and then they acted
medium.explanation: Moses called first, the Levites gathered to him, and then they carried out his command.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that all the sons of Levi gathered to Moses?
answers: They answered the call to stand with the Lord and were ready to obey Moses
They did not hear Moses’ words
They wanted to leave the camp
challenge.explanation: The text emphasizes that all the Levites gathered and then did as Moses commanded.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “a reproach among their enemies” mean in context?
answers: The people would receive praise from their friends
The people’s behavior would become a disgrace in the eyes of their opponents
The people would rise early in the morning
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses concern that the shameful act would become a lasting disgrace before Israel’s enemies.

challenge.question: Why does the passage mention “every man his brother… his companion… his neighbor”?
answers: To list the names of those killed
To show that only relatives were punished
To emphasize that the action was not limited by family or friendship
challenge.explanation: The details show that the action involved people of every relationship, without favoring relatives or friends.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that all the sons of Levi gathered to Moses?
answers: They answered the call to stand with the Lord and were ready to obey Moses
They did not hear Moses’ words
They wanted to leave the camp
questions.explanation: The text emphasizes that all the Levites gathered and then did as Moses commanded.

questions.question: What does the phrase “a reproach among their enemies” mean in context?
answers: The people would receive praise from their friends
The people’s behavior would become a disgrace in the eyes of their opponents
The people would rise early in the morning
questions.explanation: The phrase expresses concern that the shameful act would become a lasting disgrace before Israel’s enemies.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention “every man his brother… his companion… his neighbor”?
answers: To list the names of those killed
To show that only relatives were punished
To emphasize that the action was not limited by family or friendship
questions.explanation: The details show that the action involved people of every relationship, without favoring relatives or friends.

paragraphs.title: Moses Seeks Atonement for the People

easy.question: Who told the people, “Ye have sinned a great sin”?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses spoke these words to the people.

easy.question: How did Moses describe the people’s sin?
answers: A small sin
A great sin
A minor mistake
easy.explanation: Moses said, “Ye have sinned a great sin.”

easy.question: Where did Moses say he would go?
answers: To the camp
Into the wilderness
To the Lord
easy.explanation: Moses said, “Now I will go up unto the Lord.”

medium.question: When did the events in this verse take place?
answers: On the next day
Before the sin
A year later
medium.explanation: The verse begins, “And it came to pass on the morrow.”

medium.question: What did Moses hope to accomplish by going up to the Lord?
answers: Build an altar
Make atonement for the people’s sin
Punish the people
medium.explanation: Moses said he would go up to the Lord, perhaps to make atonement for their sin.

medium.question: What did Moses mean by saying, “Peradventure I shall make an atonement”?
answers: He would try to make atonement for the sin
He would flee from the sin
He would write down the sin
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses Moses’ hope or attempt to seek atonement for the people.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses saying “peradventure” rather than promising that he would certainly make atonement?
answers: He did not know the people
He knew that atonement depended on the Lord’s will
He refused to help the people
challenge.explanation: “Peradventure” expresses hope or an attempt, not certainty that Moses would succeed.

challenge.question: What order of events appears in the verse?
answers: Moses went up, and afterward the people sinned
The people sinned, and then Moses announced that he would go up
The people were forgiven, and then Moses heard about the sin
challenge.explanation: Moses first stated that the people had sinned, and then announced that he would go up to the Lord.

challenge.question: What does Moses’ address to the people reveal about his attitude toward them?
answers: He ignored their sin
He wanted to abandon them
He rebuked them while also trying to help them
challenge.explanation: Moses confronted the people about their sin but immediately offered to seek atonement for them.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses saying “peradventure” rather than promising that he would certainly make atonement?
answers: He did not know the people
He knew that atonement depended on the Lord’s will
He refused to help the people
questions.explanation: “Peradventure” expresses hope or an attempt, not certainty that Moses would succeed.

questions.question: What order of events appears in the verse?
answers: Moses went up, and afterward the people sinned
The people sinned, and then Moses announced that he would go up
The people were forgiven, and then Moses heard about the sin
questions.explanation: Moses first stated that the people had sinned, and then announced that he would go up to the Lord.

questions.question: What does Moses’ address to the people reveal about his attitude toward them?
answers: He ignored their sin
He wanted to abandon them
He rebuked them while also trying to help them
questions.explanation: Moses confronted the people about their sin but immediately offered to seek atonement for them.

paragraphs.title: Moses Confesses and Pleads for Mercy

easy.question: Who returned to the Lord?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Moses returned unto the Lord.”

easy.question: What had the people made?
answers: A stone altar
Gods of gold
A scroll of the Law
easy.explanation: Moses said that the people had made gods of gold.

easy.question: What did Moses ask to happen if the Lord would not forgive the people?
answers: The people should return to Egypt
He should be punished instead of the people
He should be blotted out of the Lord’s book
easy.explanation: Moses said, “Blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book.”

answers: He abandoned the people
He asked the Lord to forgive or bear their sin
He commanded the people to build the tabernacle
medium.explanation: After confessing the sin, Moses asked the Lord to forgive the people and bear their guilt.

medium.question: What did Moses mean by “blot me… out of thy book”?
answers: Erase me
Send me away
Preserve me
medium.explanation: Moses asked to be erased from the Lord’s book if the people would not be forgiven.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: Moses asked to be erased, and then described the people’s sin
The people asked forgiveness, and then Moses returned to the Lord
Moses returned to the Lord, confessed the sin, and then made his request
medium.explanation: Moses returned to the Lord, described the people’s sin, and then asked to be blotted out if they were not forgiven.

answers: He was willing to sacrifice himself for the people
He denied the people’s sin
He avoided responsibility for the people
challenge.explanation: Moses was willing to be erased from the Lord’s book if that would mean forgiveness for the people.

It was written by the Lord
It was written by Moses

He describes two different sins
He presents two possibilities: forgive the people or erase Moses

paragraphs.title: The Lord Responds and Provides Leadership

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses in these verses?
answers: The Lord
Aaron
The angel
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And the Lord said unto Moses.”

easy.question: Whom did the Lord say he would blot out of his book?
answers: Moses
Whoever had sinned against him
All the people
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.”

easy.question: Who would go before the people?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The angel
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Mine Angel shall go before thee.”

medium.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do after speaking about the sinner?
answers: Lead the people to the place he had spoken about
Build the tabernacle
Return to Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord told Moses to lead the people to the place he had promised.

medium.question: What does “lead the people” mean in this context?
answers: Hide them
Guide and govern them
Judge them
medium.explanation: Moses was commanded to guide the people on their journey.

medium.question: What does “in the day when I visit” refer to?
answers: The day Israel left Egypt
The day Moses died
A future time when the Lord would call the sin to account
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a future time when the Lord would deal with and judge the sin.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words, “Whosoever hath sinned against me”?
answers: Responsibility is assigned especially to the one who sinned
Only Moses sinned
No one among the people sinned
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that judgment is connected to each individual’s own sin.

challenge.question: What does the combination of “mine Angel shall go before thee” and “I will visit their sin” show?
answers: The people would receive no leadership
The journey would continue, but the sin would still be judged
The sin was immediately forgiven
challenge.explanation: The Lord continued to provide leadership while making clear that the people remained accountable for their sin.

challenge.question: What does “I will blot him out of my book” suggest?
answers: Moses would write a new book
The people would find a lost book
The sinner could lose his standing and privilege before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The image of being blotted out of a book represents the loss of standing before the Lord because of sin.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Punishes the Sin of the Calf

easy.question: Whom did the Lord plague?
answers: The people
Moses
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord plagued the people.”

easy.question: Why were the people plagued?
answers: Because they were afraid of the wilderness
Because they made the calf
Because they did not build the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse says they were punished because they made the calf.

easy.question: Who made the calf, according to the verse?
answers: Moses
The people alone
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse refers to the calf “which Aaron made.”

medium.question: What does “the Lord plagued the people” mean?
answers: He blessed the people
He struck or punished the people
He called the people
medium.explanation: In this context, “plagued” means that the Lord struck or punished the people for making the calf.

medium.question: What was the connection between making the calf and the punishment?
answers: The punishment came because the people made the calf
The punishment came because the people built the tabernacle
The punishment came before the calf was made
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly connects the punishment with the people’s making of the calf.

medium.question: What sequence fits the verse?
answers: The Lord punished the people, and then they made the calf
Aaron made the calf, the people participated in the act, and then the Lord punished them
The people were punished, and then Aaron made the calf
medium.explanation: The calf was made first, and afterward the Lord punished the people because of it.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the difference between “they made the calf” and “which Aaron made”?
answers: Only Aaron was involved
The people knew nothing about the calf
The people participated in the act, while Aaron made the calf
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions both the people’s participation and Aaron’s role in making the calf.

challenge.question: Why does the verse refer separately to the people making the calf and Aaron making it?
answers: To connect the punishment with the people’s act and identify Aaron’s role in making the calf
To describe two different peoples
To say that there were two calves
challenge.explanation: The first reference connects the punishment to the people, while the second identifies Aaron as the maker.

challenge.question: Which detail most clearly shows that the punishment was directed at the people?
answers: Aaron’s name appears at the end
The words “the people” follow immediately after “the Lord plagued”
The word “calf” appears in the middle
challenge.explanation: The wording explicitly identifies the people as those whom the Lord plagued.
